## `lr-currency-picker`

Style the label with `--lr-form-control-label-font-size`, `--lr-form-control-label-font-weight`, and
`--lr-form-control-label-color`.

Attribute `label-display` (`'visible'` default, or `'hidden'`) removes the label visually while it stays the accessible name; hint and error are unaffected (see "Hiding the label visually: `label-display`").

`labelPlacement: 'top' | 'start' = 'top'` (attribute `label-placement`, reflected) puts the label in an inline-start column sized by `--lr-form-control-label-inline-size` (default `30%`) and `--lr-form-control-label-gap` (default `var(--lr-space-m)`), returning above the field below `--lr-form-control-label-collapse-inline-size` (default `var(--lr-size-20rem)`); see "Label beside the field: `label-placement`".

A form-associated, single-currency selector with a compact ISO-code trigger and localized currency
names and symbols in its options. It composes `lr-select` (or `lr-combobox` when searchable) and `lr-option`; no additional popover,
currency-name table or optional peer is needed. Selection changes the field value only: exchange
rates, amount conversion, persistence and the application's display-currency preference belong to
the application. Selecting a currency does not change the interface language.

**Value and catalog.** `value` defaults to `''`; no currency is inferred or selected automatically.
Set `value="EUR"` when your application wants euros by default. Valid three-letter codes are trimmed
and uppercased. The default catalog contains the pinned ISO 4217 currency, fund and metal codes,
excluding the testing/no-currency codes `XTS` and `XXX`. Use `.currencies` for an ordered everyday
subset. Omitted, `undefined` or `null` restores the default catalog; `[]` means no options.

`currencies` accepts `LyraCurrencyCatalog = readonly string[] | readonly LyraCurrencyEntry[]`.
Each `LyraCurrencyEntry { readonly code: string; readonly label?: string; readonly symbol?: string;
readonly group?: string; readonly disabled?: boolean }` supplies one option. Names and symbols come from `Intl` using the field's
effective locale, with code fallbacks where display data is unavailable. Caller labels/symbols,
including explicit empty strings, override that presentation. The catalog is copied; reassign it
to change options. At most 1024 rows are examined, invalid rows are skipped, and the first valid
entry for each normalized code wins. Caller order is preserved. Names and symbols resolve once per
catalog and locale and are shared by every picker using that catalog.

A localized `catalogPickerInputLimit` notice in `part="limit"` reports original catalog positions
omitted beyond the 1,024-position inspection ceiling. Invalid and duplicate positions inside the
prefix still consume that allowance. This notice is separate from `select-option-overflow`, which
counts admitted rows outside the popup's render window. Search covers only admitted entries;
provide a narrower or replacement catalog to include omitted input. Rebinding the picker's retained
catalog snapshot preserves the notice; a fresh below-limit catalog, `[]`, or restoring defaults
clears it. Initial mounting and reconnecting are quiet; later changed input loss is politely
announced. The message supports the usual per-instance `.strings` override.

Country, currency, time-zone and unit pickers defer their option catalog until first focus or
opening. Before that, only the committed option is mounted to preserve its label; an unset picker
mounts none. Programmatic option inspection should await that interaction and update completion.
After initialization, unchanged option presentations are reused; explicit `requestUpdate()`
refreshes consumer presentation overrides. Each popup renders at most 1,000 options, exposing
omitted rows through `select-option-overflow`. Built-in catalogs remain fully available. For an
admitted catalog larger than the popup window, enable `searchable` and filter to entries outside
that initial window;
a committed tail value remains represented within the bounded popup.

**Unavailable values stay visible.** A value outside the configured catalog, a malformed nonempty
value, or a selected entry that becomes disabled is retained and marked unavailable. It fails
validation until cleared or replaced; it is never silently switched to another currency. Such a
value is not added as a selectable option. A caller's `setCustomValidity()` message takes priority.

**Field API.** `label`, `hint`, `errorText` (`error-text`) and their slots supply field chrome.
`accessibleLabel` (host attribute `aria-label`) overrides the computed field name; otherwise a label or localized Currency name
names the actual control. `placeholder` defaults to localized Select, with explicit empty strings
preserved. `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `defaultValue`, native form submission/reset,
fieldset disablement, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()` and `setCustomValidity()` follow the
shared form contracts. `size` defaults to `m`; `clearable` defaults to `false`. `focus()`, `blur()`
and `click()` forward to the visible control.

`customError: string | null = null` (attribute `custom-error`, reflected) supplies a consumer
validation message. `getForm()` returns the browser-resolved form owner, including an external
owner selected by `form`. `setCustomValidity(message)` sets or clears `customError`;
`resetValidity()` clears only that consumer error and recomputes the current required/catalog
constraints, leaving `value`, `defaultValue` and interaction state unchanged.

`topLayer` (attribute `top-layer`, reflected) defaults to `false`; enable it inside clipped or
`z-index`ed sticky headers, toolbars and native dialogs. It follows the `lr-select` `top-layer`
contract in all four catalog pickers, applies live while open, and the listbox otherwise stacks at
`var(--lr-overlay-stack-index, var(--lr-layer-dropdown))`.
An explicit `positioningStrategy` (attribute `positioning-strategy`) of `"fixed"` or `"absolute"`
overrides inherited `--lr-positioning-strategy`; with neither, the list uses `absolute` in both
modes.
Keyboard navigation and ISO-code type-ahead use the select contract by default. Set
`searchable` (default `false`) to enable a text filter matching codes, localized names, literal
labels, and regular/narrow symbols. Typing only filters; it does not change `value` or emit
selection events. A query matching the current displayed code follows the combobox convention
of showing the complete list. An empty or unmatched query never creates a currency.
`group` supplies caller-owned headings for contiguous rows; order is never rearranged.
`autocomplete='off'`, `inputMode=''` (attribute `inputmode`), `enterKeyHint=''`
(attribute `enterkeyhint`), `spellcheck=false`,
`autocapitalize=''`, and `autocorrect=true` forward native editing guidance in searchable mode.
The readonly `input: HTMLInputElement | null` exposes that native filter (null in compact mode).
After directly changing its DOM value, dispatch a native `input` event to update filtering.
Mode changes, reset and reconnect clear unfinished filtering without changing the reset default.
If the filter fails to load, `lr-load-error` fires and the compact picker remains usable.
`search-error` and `search-retry` expose the localized notice and retry action.
`--lr-form-control-invalid-border-color` themes the resting invalid border.
The popup emits `lr-show`, `lr-hide`, `lr-after-show`, `lr-after-hide`, `lr-activate`, and `lr-clear`
in both modes, following the country picker's event contract.

**Events:** A user choice or clear first dispatches the cancelable `lr-change-request`
(`detail: { value, previousValue }`, the proposed code while `value` still holds the current one).
`preventDefault()` keeps the current value and suppresses the change sequence and `lr-clear`; a
listener may instead resolve it by assigning `value` itself, which also suppresses the built-in
commit. This veto is shared by all four catalog pickers. An accepted user choice or clear updates
`value` synchronously, then emits exactly one `input`, `lr-input`, `change`, `lr-change` sequence. The prefixed details are
`LyraCurrencyChangeDetail { readonly value: string; readonly previousValue: string }`.
Re-selecting the current code, programmatic
updates, resets, locale changes and catalog replacements emit no change event. Native `focus` and
`blur` relay once. The cancelable `lr-invalid` alias follows native validation.
`lr-show` proposes opening the options and can be vetoed. `lr-hide` proposes closing them and can
be vetoed during an ordinary close. `lr-after-show` and `lr-after-hide` report completion.
`lr-activate` reports activation of an enabled option, including reselection. `lr-clear` reports
that the clear action emptied the selection. `lr-load-error` reports a failure to load the optional
searchable picker. The compact control remains available.

**Slots:** `label`, `hint`, `error` — custom field copy. There is no option/default content slot;
bind `currencies` to supply rows.

**CSS parts:** `form-control`, `form-control-label`, `hint`, `error`, `limit` (original catalog
input-loss notice);
`select-trigger`, `select-display-input`, `select-listbox`, `select-option`, `select-option-overflow`, `select-option-sub`,
`select-clear-button`, `select-group-label`, `search-error`, and `search-retry`. Both composed controls
preserve their shared part names and inherit shared form-control and surface tokens.

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@aceshooting/lyra-ui/components/lr-currency-picker.js';

  const picker = document.querySelector('lr-currency-picker');
  picker.currencies = ['EUR', 'USD', 'GBP', 'CHF', 'JPY', 'CAD', 'AUD'];
  picker.addEventListener('lr-change', ({ detail }) => {
    console.log(detail.value, detail.previousValue);
  });
</script>

<lr-currency-picker name="currency" label="Display currency" value="EUR"></lr-currency-picker>
```
